prompt_md: You walk 1 km in a random direction, then 1 km in a new, independent random direction. What is the chance you end up more than 1 km from where you started?
prompt_short: Two 1 km legs in random directions. Chance you end over 1 km from start?
hint_md: Only the turn between the two legs matters.
explain_intuition_md: Only the turn between the legs matters, and it's equally likely to be anything from straight ahead to a U-turn. You end up within 1 km only after a sharp turn of more than 120 degrees, a third of the range. A 90-degree turn already leaves you 1.41 km away, so 'more than 1 km' is the usual case.
explain_math_md: With angle $\phi$ between the legs uniform on $[0^\circ, 180^\circ]$, the distance is $2\cos(\phi/2)$: $$2\cos(\phi/2) > 1 \iff \phi < 120^\circ, \quad P = \frac{120}{180} = \tfrac23$$
